findings.title: Only one of the claimed slice-level transitions has an insertion point
findings.description:
The document says "V1 implements only the four slice-level transitions" (Initiative-level gating section). The config sample has only three slice-level gates (`pre-tasks`, `pre-implementation`, `pre-advance`). The fourth, `pre-slice-plan`, is initiative-level and deferred. So the count is wrong to begin with.

The design itself covers only `pre-advance`:
- The Gate insertion point section puts one branch between Priority 5 and Priority 6.
- `pending-review` is defined as "tasks complete … no review artifact present".

`pre-tasks` would need a check of the `slice` review before Priority 4 (`needs-tasks`, `WorkflowNavigator.ts:224`). `pre-implementation` would need a check of the `tasks` review before Priority 5 (`:235`). Neither branch is described, and a slice in `needs-tasks` cannot hold a "tasks complete" status. One fix is to cut v1 to `pre-advance` only. The other is to specify all three insertion points and redefine the status values so they don't assume tasks are complete.

findings.title: The existing frontmatter parser cannot read the slice 300 contract safely
findings.description:
The document never says which parser reads review frontmatter. The only one in the codebase is `parseFrontmatter` (`packages/core/src/introspection/parsers/frontmatterParser.ts:9-49`). It returns a flat `Record<string, string>` (`FrontmatterData`, `types.ts:41-43`) and splits every line on its first colon, ignoring indentation. Three consequences:

1. **Nested fields can overwrite `verdict` and `score`.** `criteria` and `provenance` are nested structures. Any nested `verdict:` or `score:` key inside them silently replaces the top-level value. List items turn into junk keys like `- name`. The claim that CF "carries `criteria` and `provenance` as opaque fields" can't hold: they are destroyed, not carried.
2. **Parse failures can't be reported.** The parser "never throws" and returns `{found:false}` for a missing file, malformed YAML, or an unreadable file alike. Technical Considerations promises "the rationale … names the parse failure explicitly", which this API cannot support.
3. **`score` arrives as a string.** "Float 0–100" needs a parse step and its own failure policy.

The document needs to name a real YAML parser for review files, or extend this one. It also needs a result type that tells absent, malformed and unreadable apart.

findings.title: "Lexicographically last = most recent" is false for this naming convention
findings.description:
The pattern is `NNN-review.{type}.{name}.md`, and `{name}` is a descriptive slug, not a timestamp. Two code reviews of slice 210 named `…code.api-layer.md` and `…code.refactor-pass.md` sort alphabetically, so a stale FAIL can beat a newer PASS, or the reverse. Re-running a review with the same name overwrites the file, which makes multiple matches rare but leaves the rule unexplained.

Choose a meaningful key, for example a `dateCreated`/`dateUpdated` field in the frontmatter or a provenance timestamp. Alternatively, treat multiple matches as an explicit `UNKNOWN` with a warning. Don't call alphabetical order "most recent".

findings.title: The `recommendation` field has no stable vocabulary for Amoeba to depend on
findings.description:
`NextAction.recommendation` (`types.ts:280-289`) holds human-readable prose, built dynamically. Examples: `Advance to slice ${n}: ${name}` and `Continue implementation — N tasks remaining` (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:240,253`). Adding the bare tokens `"review"` and `"blocked"` mixes machine values into a prose field. Runners still can't recognise the existing `advance` state without matching strings, which conflicts with Design Goals ("without parsing recommendation strings"). The `auto_advance` section also refers to "an `advance` recommendation", and no such literal exists.

Add an optional discriminated field to `NextAction`, such as `action: 'review' | 'blocked' | 'advance' | …`, defined once as an `as const` map per the TypeScript rules. Keep `recommendation` as prose. The field is additive and doesn't break the "don't change `NextAction`" constraint in spirit.

findings.title: A single `review` slot with a config-driven type mixes config into the pure detector
findings.description:
`detectDocuments(projectPath, sliceIndex)` (`documentDetector.ts:46`) has no access to config, and every other slot is a fixed pattern. The proposal scans "for the … configured reviewType" into a single `review: string | null`. That brings config into the detector. It also can't represent the several review types one slice needs once more than one gate is active: `slice`, `tasks` and `code`.

Have the detector return every review match keyed by type, for example `reviews: Record<string, string[]>`. Let the gate logic in `WorkflowNavigator` pick the type from config.

findings.title: Threshold and unknown-policy value sets are never defined, and are spelled inconsistently
findings.description:
The doc says it will fail fast on invalid config, but never lists the allowed values:
- `review_threshold` is shown as `"pass"` and `"concerns"`. The text says CONCERNS clears "if threshold = concerns or lower", but no lower value is defined. Is `"fail"` allowed, meaning everything passes?
- `review_unknown_as` defaults to `"fail"`. Technical Considerations uses `"concern"` (singular, unlike `"concerns"`). The Slice status section implies a third value that maps to `pending-review` ("treats it as pending").

Define both as closed sets in one constant (`ConfigKeyDefinition.enum` already exists, `ConfigKeys.ts:5`). Specify which `review_unknown_as` value produces `pending-review` and which produces `review-failed`. Without this, the validator can't be written and the "full decision matrix" test in the Anticipated Slices section has no specification.

findings.title: The new consistency rule conflicts with the existing auto-fix that checks plan boxes on task completion
findings.description:
`ruleTaskVsPlan` (`ConsistencyChecker.ts:269-283`) flags "tasks complete but plan unchecked" as fixable. With `workflow.auto_fix = true` it checks the slice-plan box as soon as tasks finish, before any review exists. The new rule then fires a warning ("marked complete in the slice plan but its required review artifact is absent") about a state the checker created itself.

There are now two definitions of "complete": the gate uses task completion and the checker uses the plan checkbox. When review gating is on, `ruleTaskVsPlan` should not auto-check the plan entry until the gate clears. Alternatively, the review rule should key on task completion, as the navigator does. The document should say which.

findings.title: Nested `review_gates` config is deferred, yet slice 1 depends on it
findings.description:
`ConfigKeyDefinition` (`ConfigKeys.ts:1-7`) supports only `string | boolean | number` scalars. The choice between nested tables and dotted keys is pushed to slice design, but the first anticipated slice must deliver "per-gate override structure". The choice also affects validation: dotted keys mean four gates × two fields of free-form keys, each needing its own validator, plus rejection of unknown gate names as the fail-fast principle requires. It also affects worktree resolution (initiative 180), which presumably merges scalar keys.

This load-bearing decision belongs in the architecture. Given the project's "resist complexity" rule, a lighter option for v1 is to drop per-gate overrides. Only `pre-advance` is actually gated in v1, and the global `review_threshold` plus a single `review_type` covers it.

findings.title: The review gate is a new step that the existing broad `catch` can silently skip
findings.description: `deriveSliceStatus` wraps all detection in a bare `catch { return base; }` (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:494-496`), which yields `no-active-slice`. If review discovery or parsing throws inside this block, the gate doesn't block and doesn't explain itself; the slice status just collapses. That breaks the "must not silently pass" principle in Technical Considerations. The design should say that the review step returns typed `UNKNOWN` results rather than throwing, or that it runs outside this catch.

findings.title: There is no way out of `review-failed` that CF can see
findings.description:
Reconciliation is placed "above CF's layer" ("a bounded judge dismissing findings, human decision"). But CF reads only the artifact on disk, so the only way to clear the gate is a new artifact with a passing verdict. A human override, or a judge dismissing findings, has no representation: no frontmatter field, no config, no CLI command. A team would have to hand-edit `verdict:` in a Squadron-owned file, which conflicts with "CF must not … reinterpret this schema".

The `blocked` recommendation also carries no `suggestedCommand`. At minimum, name how an override is expressed, or state that a re-review is the only path.

findings.title: The Current State section misdescribes `SliceStatus`
findings.description: `SliceStatus` is an interface whose `status` field is a string-literal union (`types.ts:254-263`), not an enum. That union also includes `no-active-slice`, which the doc omits. The citations of `:83–300` and `:446–497` are correct. This doesn't change the design, but slice authors should extend the union, not look for an enum.

findings.title: The worktree-scope requirement isn't carried into any slice
findings.description: Related Work says `workflow.review_*` "should be resolvable at worktree scope" using the 180 resolution chain. None of the Anticipated Slices includes this work or a test for it. Either add it to the config-keys slice or drop the requirement.
